67628-youth-and-life.title: Youth And Life
67628-youth-and-life.creator: Unknown
67628-youth-and-life.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. rdinated into the orderly and precise movements of his elders,--so the youth suddenly born into a confusion of ideas and appeals and traditions responds in the most chaotic way to this new spiritual world, and only gradually learns to find his way about in it, and get his thoughts and feelings into some kind of order.

arxiv-1912-00050.title: Spectra of Compact Quotients of the Oscillator Group
arxiv-1912-00050.creator: Mathias FISCHER and Ines KATH
arxiv-1912-00050.description: Abstract This paper is a contribution to harmonic analysis of compact solvmanifolds. We consider the four-dimensional oscillator group Osc 1 {\rm Osc}_{1} , which is a semi-direct product of the three-dimensional Heisenberg group and the real line. We classify the lattices of Osc 1 {\rm Osc}_{1} up to inner automorphisms of Osc 1 {\rm Osc}_{1} .

arxiv-2208-13505.title: Dephasing and Decorrelation of Spins in a Disordered Environment
arxiv-2208-13505.creator: Shreyas Raman, Subroto Mukerjee
arxiv-2208-13505.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Shreyas Raman, Subroto Mukerjee. Dephasing of spins is a major roadblock to scaling up the size of quantum computing systems. We explore the possibility of utilizing highly disordered environments which are in the Many-Body Localized phase to arrest this dephasing.

arxiv-2301-05605.title: Differentially Private Continual Releases of Streaming Frequency Moment Estimations
arxiv-2301-05605.creator: Alessandro Epasto <aepasto@google.com>
arxiv-2301-05605.description: Abstract The streaming model of computation is a popular approach for working with large-scale data. In this setting, there is a stream of items and the goal is to compute the desired quantities (usually data statistics) while making a single pass through the stream and using as little space as possible.

arxiv-2303-13639.title: Hemodynamic Effects of Entry and Exit Tear Size in Aortic Dissection Evaluated with In Vitro Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Fluid-Structure Interaction Simulation
arxiv-2303-13639.creator: Judith Zimmermann, Kathrin Bäumler, Michael Loecher, Tyler E. Cork, Alison L. Marsden, Daniel B. Ennis, Dominik Fleischmann
arxiv-2303-13639.description: Abstract Understanding the complex interplay between morphologic and hemodynamic features in aortic dissection is critical for risk stratification and for the development of individualized therapy. This work evaluates the effects of entry and exit tear size on the hemodynamics in type B aortic dissection by comparing fluid-structure interaction (FSI) simulations with in vitro 4D-flow magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

arxiv-2308-14938.title: Entropy-based Guidance of Deep Neural Networks for Accelerated Convergence and Improved Performance
arxiv-2308-14938.creator: Mackenzie J. Meni, Ryan T. White, Michael L. Mayo, Kevin R. Pilkiewicz
arxiv-2308-14938.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mackenzie J. Meni, Ryan T. White, Michael L. Mayo, Kevin R. Pilkiewicz. Neural networks have dramatically increased our capacity to learn from large, high-dimensional datasets across innumerable disciplines. However, their decisions are not easily interpretable, their computational costs are high, and building and training them are not straightforward processes. To add structure to these efforts, we derive new mathematical results to efficiently measure the changes in entropy as fully-connected and convolutional neural networks process data.

arxiv-2402-18333.title: On the simulation of quantum multimeters
arxiv-2402-18333.creator: Andreas Bluhm, Leevi Leppäjärvi, Ion Nechita
arxiv-2402-18333.description: Abstract . In the quest for robust and universal quantum devices, the notion of simulation plays a crucial role, both from a theoretical and from an applied perspective. In this work, we go beyond the simulation of quantum channels and quantum measurements, studying what it means to simulate a collection of measurements, which we call a multimeter.

arxiv-2412-14820.title: Ultrastable optical frequency dissemination over a branching passive optical network using CDMA
arxiv-2412-14820.creator: Rodrigo González Escudero, 1 Sougandh Kannoth Mavila, 1 and Jeroen C. J. Koelemeij *,1
arxiv-2412-14820.description: Abstract We demonstrate a technique for ultrastable optical frequency dissemination in a branching passive optical network using code-division multiple access (CDMA). In our protocol, each network user employs a unique pseudo-random sequence to rapidly change the optical frequency among many distinct frequencies.

arxiv-2510-03690.title: From Moments to Models: Graphon Mixture-Aware Mixup and Contrastive Learning
arxiv-2510-03690.creator: Ali Azizpour, Reza Ramezanpour, Ashutosh Sabharwal, Santiago Segarra
arxiv-2510-03690.description: Abstract Real-world graph datasets often consist of mixtures of populations, where graphs are generated from multiple distinct underlying distributions. However, modern representation learning approaches, such as graph contrastive learning (GCL) and augmentation methods like Mixup, typically overlook this mixture structure.

pmc-11378773.title: Existing evidence on the effects of photovoltaic panels on biodiversity: a systematic map with critical appraisal of study validity
pmc-11378773.creator: Alix Lafitte, Romain Sordello, Dakis-Yaoba Ouédraogo, Chloé Thierry, Geoffroy Marx, Jérémy Froidevaux, Bertrand Schatz, Christian Kerbiriou, Philippe Gourdain, Yorick Reyjol
pmc-11378773.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundTo phase out fossil fuels and reach a carbon–neutral future, solar energy and notably photovoltaic (PV) installations are being rapidly scaled up. Unlike other types of renewable energies such as wind and hydroelectricity, evidence on the effects of PV installations on biodiversity has been building up only fairly recently and suggests that they may directly impact ecosystems and species through, for instance, habitat change and loss, mortality, behaviour alteration or population displacements.

pmc-11518694.title: Comprehensive single‐cell profiling of monocytes in HLA‐B27‐positive ankylosing spondylitis with acute anterior uveitis
pmc-11518694.creator: Huan Li, Xueming Ju, Lixin Zhang, Jing Zhu, Jing Zhang, Jialing Xiao, Ting Wang, Weijia Wu, Liang Wang, Chengzi Gan, Xiangmei Li, Yutong Wei, Siyu Zhu, Yu Zhou, Bolin Deng, Ning Xiao, Bo Gong
pmc-11518694.description: Acute anterior uveitis (AAU) is a common extra‐articular manifestation of ankylosing spondylitis (AS), particularly in patients positive for the human leucocyte antigen (HLA)‐B27 genetic marker. To explore the underlying mechanisms of HLA‐B27+ AS‐associated AAU, we employed single‐cell RNA sequencing to profile the transcriptomes of peripheral blood mononuclear cells in three HLA‐B27+ AS‐associated AAU patients and three healthy controls (HCs).

pmc-11692819.title: THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY ACTIVITIES AND COGNITIVE DOMAINS OF COMMUNITY DWELLING OLDER ADULTS
pmc-11692819.creator: Erh-Chi Hsu, Eric Jutkowitz, Kali Thomas
pmc-11692819.description: While prior research has established a relationship between digital technology use and improved cognitive function among older adults, the impacts of different technology activities on specific cognitive domains remain underexplored. This study examines associations between various technology activities and cognitive trajectories in community-dwelling older adults without dementia.

pmc-12475835.title: Molecular characterization, antimicrobial resistance profiling, and biofilm analysis of Salmonella isolates from dead-in-shell embryonated eggs
pmc-12475835.creator: Swagat Khanal, Himal Luitel, Sujan Adhikari, Aakash Marasini, Rebanta Kumar Bhattarai
pmc-12475835.description: This study investigates the molecular characterization, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) profiling, and biofilm formation of Salmonella isolates from dead-in-shell embryonated eggs collected from 15 hatcheries in Bharatpur, Chitwan. A total of 210 samples were analyzed using cultural, biochemical, and molecular techniques, including PCR for virulence gene detection. The study revealed a prevalence rate of 11.

pmc-13186804.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals HMGA2 involvement in neoplastic aggressiveness and endothelial cell senescence in chondrosarcoma
pmc-13186804.creator: Shenglin Wang, Shuting Lu, Xinwen Wang, Hongxiang Wei, Huarong Zhang, Weixin Zhou, Jie Lin, Xueyi Huang, Fude Liang, Zhaoyang Wu, Jianhua Lin, Xiaopei Shen, Lu Ao
pmc-13186804.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AbstractChondrosarcoma (CHS) is a malignant bone tumor resistant to adjuvant treatment, with high-grade patients suffering an unfavorable prognosis. Therefore, a deeper insight into the tumor microenvironment is essential for developing effective treatments for advanced CHS. To decipher the cellular heterogeneity between CHS with differential malignancy and benign cartilage tumors, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on clinical specimens of high- and low-grade CHS, endochondroma and paratumoral tissues. The findings of transcriptional characteristics were validated by the bioinformatics analyses of public bulk datasets.

pmc-13354665.title: Crossbreeding crioula and lacaune for milking productive performance and milk composition of crioula × lacaune crossbred ewes under pampa conditions
pmc-13354665.creator: Eduarda Arteche Berón da Fontoura, Melina Calegaro Tamiozzo, Leonardo de Melo Menezes, Rafael Fernandes Leite, Carla Joice Härter
pmc-13354665.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Crioula sheep are used in tough conditions in South America, especially in the Pampa Biome, and breeding them with dairy sheep may be a good strategy for producers to improve dairy products without losing the hardiness of the sheep. Thus, the objective of this study was to evaluate the milk production characteristics of Lacaune, Crioula, and Lacaune × Crioula (F1) ewes. Thirty-seven ewes were used: 14 Lacaune, 14 Crioulas, and 9 F1 (crossbred) ewes from the same producer.

pmc-13368402.title: Functionalizing biomaterials for osseointegration – microRNAs at the crossroads of bone formation and immune modulation
pmc-13368402.creator: Mandana Azari, Elena Della Bella, Britt Wildemann
pmc-13368402.description: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) play an important role in post-transcriptional gene regulation by binding to messenger RNA and thereby modulating protein synthesis and affecting cellular functions such as proliferation and apoptosis. In bone biology, miRNAs influence osseointegration, a process vital to the long-term success of orthopaedic implants.

pmc-13471193.title: Molecular Detection and Subtype Characterization of Blastocystis spp. in Symptomatic Children Using PCR and Sequencing
pmc-13471193.creator: Samaneh Boulaghi, Amirali Reihani, BiBi Razieh Hosseini Farash, Yousef Sharifi, Omid Ahmadi, Alireza Samadi, Ghodratollah Salehi Sangani, Mohsen Najjari, Fariba Berenji, Mehdi Zarean
pmc-13471193.description: Background:Blastocystis spp. is a globally distributed intestinal protozoan that infects humans and various animals. This protozoan is a common pathogen among humans and animals and can be transmitted from animal species to humans. Therefore, the present study aimed to identify and characterize Blastocystis sub-types in children with gastrointestinal symptoms using PCR and sequencing.

pmc-13505126.title: Development and multi-center validation of a machine learning‑based prediction model for mortality in tumor-related sepsis

pmc-13558797.title: Computer-assisted surgical anatomical mapping of the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerves. Is there a safe zone for surgery?
pmc-13558797.creator: Lisette C Langenberg, Alexander Poublon, Michiel Zuidam
pmc-13558797.description: The medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve has a large variation in number and course of its branches. Computer-assisted surgical anatomical mapping of the nerve branches demonstrates no safe zone for surgery around the medial epicondyle of the elbow. The cutaneous nerves around the elbow are known to have variable courses among individuals (Kwon, 2020).
